title: Sep 26 Results + Sep 27 Preview: Nine Wins, Four Losses—I'll Take That Split
summary: Sep 26 brought a solid 9-4 day. Tomorrow's top pick heads back to Washington.

content.value:
## Another Day at the Office

You know, I've been doing this long enough to recognize when the model's humming along nicely. A 9-4 record on a September Friday? That's the kind of day that reminds you why we trust the numbers. Not perfect—never is—but a 69.2% hit rate keeps the lights on and then some.

## The Wins That Mattered

The Dodgers at 63% confidence? That one felt right from the jump. Same with the Rays pulling through in Philly at 61%—Tampa's been scrappy all year, even when nobody's watching. The Rangers squeaking past the Twins at 51% was about as close as they come, but a win's a win in this business.

Braves took care of business in Miami, Brewers handled the Cardinals at home, and Detroit did what they needed to do against Pittsburgh. These September games, they've got their own rhythm. Teams either playing for something or playing spoiler.

## Where We Missed

The Nationals, Jays, Royals, and Sox didn't cooperate. Can't say I'm shocked—three of those were essentially coin flips, and Toronto at 60% was probably the one that stings most. But that's baseball in late September. Rosters are shuffled, motivations vary, and sometimes the better team just doesn't show up.

## Tomorrow's Top Pick: Back to D.C.

Here's the thing about the Mets-Nationals series—we liked Washington yesterday at 50-50 and missed. Now the model's flipping the script for Saturday, favoring New York at 52%. It's still essentially a toss-up, but there's a reason for the lean.

Sean Manaea gets the ball for the Mets. He's been steady, if unspectacular, down this stretch. On the other side, DJ Herz takes the mound for Washington. The kid's got arm talent, no question, but consistency has been the issue all year.

content.sub: 52% win probability · Manaea vs Herz · @ Nationals

content.value:
## The Veteran's Take

I've covered enough Mets-Nationals games to write a book. This late in the season, with both teams likely out of contention by now in 2026, it comes down to execution. Manaea's the safer bet—he knows how to navigate a lineup, doesn't beat himself. Herz is still learning those lessons.

At 52%, we're not breaking the bank here. But in a tight slate, sometimes the marginal edge is all you need. The Mets have been in these spots before. They know how to grind out September road wins when the pressure's off but professional pride is still on the line.

Check back tomorrow. We'll see if the model's got the Mets-Nats dynamic figured out this time.
